summary: Optimize what-if ROI estimates show unrealistically high savings (cache warm-rate assumed ~100%)
description:
Customer reports that Optimize "Enable prefix caching" recommendation shows 65–80% cost savings for their chat workload, which they believe is not achievable given their prompt variability and low cache hit rate.

Issue summary:
- Optimize UI what-if ROI for caching shows very large savings.
- Customer believes actual cache hit rate is low (~10–25%) and that estimates should reflect warm-up / low reuse.

Impact:
- Customer questions credibility of Optimize ROI and Redwood cost methodology.
- Risk: sales cycle slowdown and additional CS time.

Customer context:
- Arcadia LegalTech is evaluating Optimize for a regulated workload with heavy system prompts + per-user context. They report high prompt diversity (low expected prefix reuse).

Observed behavior:
- Optimize ROI card shows large delta in "cache savings" with little/no downside.
- When customer runs A/B manually, realized savings are materially lower.

Suspected root cause (initial triage):
- Cache warm-rate / cache re-use assumptions in what-if projection appear to be effectively set to 1.0 (100% warm), even when workload is not warm.
- Potential mismatch between Optimize input field naming and Cost Model API what-if parameter semantics.

Example (from customer screenshot and our reproduction in prod via internal tooling):
- Baseline: ~2.1M tokens/day, p95 latency steady, no caching enabled.
- What-if: caching enabled; estimated savings ~72%.
- Request appears to omit an explicit cache warm-rate / warmness parameter; backend defaults to a best-case assumption.

Requested outcome:
1) Correct the default assumptions so what-if projections are conservative unless provided workload measurements.
2) Clarify schema semantics and document which fields are required vs optional for cache what-if accuracy.
3) Provide customer-facing explanation and updated estimate using their real cache hit/warm-rate.

Internal notes:
- This ticket is specifically about what-if ROI estimates being optimistic, not invoice mismatch. See SUP-31844 for Console vs invoice discrepancies.

2026-02-19 10:22 PT — Aditya Rao: Proposed customer message: "Earlier ROI assumed steady-state warm cache; using your measured hit rate, estimated savings are ~15–25% depending on route" + note that Optimize will be updated to ask for/workload-estimate cache warmness and display a range.

resolution: Optimize what-if ROI was inflated due to a misconfigured default cache warm-rate assumption (UI defaulted warm_rate=1.0). Customer was provided corrected estimates using telemetry-derived cache hit rate (~18% avg; ~10–25% range). Optimize updated to omit warm-rate unless explicitly set or derived from telemetry; schema/semantics documentation to be clarified by platform.
workaround: Until the UI fix rolled out, support recommended setting cache warm-rate explicitly to a conservative value (0.1–0.25) in the advanced what-if configuration and interpreting results as steady-state only if the workload is known to be warm.
follow_ups: Update Cost Model API schema docs to explicitly define cache warm-rate semantics and omission/default behavior (owner: Ethan Park).
Add Cost Model API what-if response warnings/assumptions so Optimize can display them (owner: Ethan Park / Jonas Weber).
Add guardrails to prevent best-case defaults in what-if paths and require explicit user intent for warm_rate > 0.9 (owner: Platform team; aligns with policy guardrails work).
Add a small QA test fixture for caching what-if with warm_rate omitted to prevent regression (owner: Leila Farouk).
